qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Switching costs exist in high-reliability segments (medical, automotive, data center infrastructure) via tooling, certifications, and product redesign barriers. However, Flex lacks pricing power above inflation; contracts are predominantly cost-plus pass-through arrangements where OEM customers command procurement leverage, keeping gross margins at 7-9% and GAAP operating margins at 4-5%.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (Rejected – G3 Moat & Pricing). Contract electronics manufacturing services (EMS) provider operating in a structurally thin-margin, commoditized industry. While specialized engineering and certifications create modest switching costs, Flex lacks autonomous pricing power above inflation; GAAP operating margins remain thin at ~4.5%, and pricing is constrained by aggressive OEM procurement and global EMS competitors.
qualitative.evidence: FY24-FY25 revenue of $25.8B-$26.4B with GAAP operating margins of 4.4%-4.5% and gross margins of 7.6%-8.6%. While 10-year median ROIC (~12.8%-15%) is buoyed by high asset turns and working capital velocity, contract manufacturing dynamics prevent independent markup expansion. Contracts operate on cost-plus/pass-through terms where OEMs retain the economic surplus, dual-source programs, and impose periodic price-down pressures.
